policies.title: Capture Gold annotation policy — overall completion
policies.summary: A reviewer judges one overall ExtractionResult per source message and marks it accepted, edited, or rejected. A message containing more than one commitment is judged on its primary commitment; there is no way to record the secondary one. This is the policy the canonical 50-record first pass was made under.

policies.title: Capture Gold annotation policy — explicit per-item separation
policies.summary: Multi-commitment sources must be separated into ordered per-item Gold with explicit source-language segments and code-point offsets, recorded in data/review/per-item-gold.jsonl. A combined single-commitment completion is no longer acceptable for such a source. Introduced by the remediation round between the first and second calibration passes; this registry exists because that change was previously unrecorded.

changedRules.statement: A source containing more than one commitment may not be accepted as a single combined completion. It requires ordered per-item Gold, one item per commitment.
Per-item segments are exact source-language substrings with end-exclusive Unicode code-point offsets in logical order. The reviewer selects them; tooling never proposes or pre-populates a boundary.

policies.title: Capture Gold annotation policy — temporal resolution and edit threshold
policies.summary: Corrective guidance from the issue #5 root-cause analysis. Closes the two guidance gaps that produced the remaining calibration disagreements: how a relative temporal expression is resolved, and when a title rewrite requires an 'edited' decision rather than 'accepted'.

changedRules.statement: A relative temporal expression is always resolved against the record's own reference_time and timezone, never against the annotation session's wall clock. If a resolved value's date does not follow from reference_time, the annotation is wrong.

A date-only expression such as 'tomorrow' or 'מחר' with no clock time is recorded as a date-only localTimeSpec. It is never recorded as a dueAt with an invented time, and never dropped to null — dropping it silently discards a temporal fact the source stated.
A title rewrite requires the 'edited' decision only when the proposed title changes meaning, drops a named entity, or drops a project identifier. Rewording that preserves all three is 'accepted'.

primaryCalibrationCategory is assigned by commitment count first. A source containing more than one commitment is categorised multiple_commitments even when it also code-switches, so the multi-commitment stratum is not under-sampled by a competing label.
